C8A79-f19.summary: Return of provisions in the king's and the merchants' stores on 1 November 1780: the situation is precarious, new supplies must come lest the colony be forced to buy for itself, the merchants' stores slightly refilled by two ships of the convoy and a neutral.
C8A79-f19.en: [I have the honour to send you] the state of the provisions on hand in the king's stores and in [those] of the merchants on the 1st of this month of November. You will see that it is as [...] as can be. [May we] receive new supplies [promptly], [otherwise it would be] prejudicial to the interests of his [majesty] that we should be forced to make them in the colony. The merchants' stores are somewhat supplied by the return of two ships of the convoy and the arrival of a neutral, but consumption is so considerable that our situation in this respect is still infinitely precarious.

C8A79-f70.summary: Troop return for Martinique, Dominica and Grenada, Saint Vincent's return of April only, du Montet's of May still missing; Bouillé will send 400-500 men to Grenada, and the Martinique regiment is 359 men short and needs recruits.
C8A79-f70.en: [I have the honour to send you] the state of the situation of the troops of Martinique, [of] the garrison of Dominica and [of] Grenada on the 1st of this month, and that of the garrison of Saint Vincent on the 1st of last April, not having yet received M. du Montet's state for the 1st of May. I intend to send [shortly] to Grenada four to five hundred men more [to] bring its garrison to seventeen or eighteen hundred men. The garrison of Saint Vincent is sufficient because of the [...] of the [...] which supply [...] the Caribs whom I have armed. The Martinique regiment is short of three hundred and fifty-nine men to bring it up to strength, and it is very important to send it recruits.

C8A81-f114.summary: Defence letter at the end of 1782: all colonies in a state of defence with six months' food, only 2,000 regulars left on Martinique, ships sent to cruise off Barbados to cover the convoy from New England and the arriving squadron, despatches for Trinidad; the writer says his presence will be useless if he is not employed in the coming operations.
C8A81-f114.en: I was to sail [...] with the Amphion and some frigates and troops to capture a convoy that the English were assembling at Tortola [...]. I am prepared for every eventuality: I have had time to put all the king's colonies in a state of defence; they are perfectly supplied with munitions of war and provisions, having no less than six months' food; I have sent reinforcements of troops and munitions of every kind to all of them. You will judge from the state of the garrisons that I send you that, apart from Martinique, where only two thousand regular troops remain, but for which I have [no] fear, they all have sufficient and proportionate garrisons. Grenada alone would have needed two or three hundred more men, and to make up for them I have sent the ship the Experiment, which is of no use here and whose troops and crew can join the garrison in case of siege.

C8A78-f123.summary: The clerks' interlinear decipherment of a letter about the fortifications of Guadeloupe, written above every group; paired group by group it gave the first 77 values of the key.

C8A78-f3.summary: Glossed letter of 6 May 1779; its number-gloss pairs, together with those of f. 31 (8 March 1779), extend the key.

C8A78-f31.summary: Glossed troop return of 8 March 1779 (heavy ink show-through): number-gloss pairs for the key.

C8A77-f88.summary: The monthly troop return after the capture of Dominica, read first by Brice Dudout; the decode here is shown to check that the key reads it.

C8A77-f101.summary: Cover note of the next return and its enclosure; the decode here is shown to check that the key reads it (the enclosure table is in table1778_f101.txt).

system: Numerical nomenclator, values 1-845 so far, mixing letters, syllables and whole words (and place names with their article: 428 = la Guadeloupe); the same code in 1778 and 1779 (Bouillé). Not the 1761 Windward Islands code (max 696) and not the 1765 d'Ennery…
